units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 7:6:7">Y. Dem. VII, 26ᶜ</cite> top <he>נוטל שני תישועין ות׳ של ת׳ וכ׳</he> he takes twice nine-tenths (of ten), and one-ninth of nine-tenths, which makes ten for the first tithe, and nine for the second. But why not say ‘nineteen’? Said R. Z., ‘the words of the wise and their riddles’.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 7:6:7">Ib.</cite> [read:] <he>הרוצה להכניס … נוטל על כל תאינה ותאינה שני תישועין ות׳ של ת׳ שהן עשרים ושלש וארבעה תישועין של תאינח</he> he who wishes to bring into his house one hundred figs available for use, must count for each fig (an addition of) two-ninths and one-ninth of one-ninth, which makes (an addition of) twenty-three figs and four-ninths of a fig (23, and 4/9 as nearest to 37/81).—Pl. <he>תִּישּׁוּעִין</he>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 2:5:2">Y. Erub. II, 20ᵇ</cite> <he>צא מהן ארבעה ת׳ … נשתייר שם תשעח עשר תלתותין חסר תשוע</he> (not <he>תלתולין</he>) deduct (from 6 2/3) four-ninths for the four sides, and there remain nineteen thirds less one-ninth (= 6 2/9).
